questions.q: In the reaction R → P the concentration of the reactant falls from 0.03 M to 0.02 M in 25 minutes. What is the average rate?
In the reaction 2HI → H₂ + I₂, which relation is correct?
questions.explain: 2 mol of HI give 1 mol of H₂, so the rate of disappearance of HI is twice the rate of formation of H₂: −(1/2)Δ[HI]/Δt = Δ[H₂]/Δt.

questions.q: What is the overall order of the reaction with rate = k [A]^{1/2} [B]^{3/2}?
What is the unit of the rate constant of a first order reaction?
In 2NO + O₂ → 2NO₂, doubling [NO] while keeping [O₂] fixed makes the rate four times. What is the order with respect to NO?
Which of the following is NOT a possible value of molecularity?
questions.explain: Molecularity is always a whole number (1, 2 or 3); it cannot be zero or a fraction. Order can be.

questions.q: For a first order reaction k = 0.0693 min^{−1}. What is the half-life?
A first order reaction has t_{½} = 20 min. How long will it take for 75 % of the reactant to be used up?
questions.explain: When 75 % is used up, 25 % remains = (1/2)², i.e. two half-lives = 40 min.

questions.q: In a zero order reaction, what happens to the half-life if [R]₀ is doubled?
questions.explain: In zero order t_{½} = [R]_{0}/2k, so it is proportional to [R]_{0}.

questions.q: Which graph is a straight line for a first order reaction?
questions.explain: ln[R] = ln[R]₀ − kt, so ln[R] against t is a straight line (slope = −k).

questions.q: By the general rule, by roughly what factor does the rate constant increase for a 10 °C rise in temperature?
questions.explain: For many reactions k roughly doubles for a 10 K rise, because the number of molecules with energy equal to or greater than E_a roughly doubles.

questions.q: What is the slope of the graph of ln k against 1/T?
questions.explain: ln k = ln A − (E_a/R)(1/T); so the slope = −E_a/R and the intercept = ln A.

questions.q: Which statement about a catalyst is correct?
options: It lowers the activation energy and does not change the equilibrium constant
It can make a non-spontaneous reaction occur
It speeds up only the forward reaction
questions.explain: A catalyst provides a path of lower E_a; it does not change ΔG, ΔH or K, and speeds up the forward and reverse reactions equally.

questions.q: According to collision theory, what is needed for a collision to be effective?
options: Both enough energy and proper orientation
questions.explain: In an effective collision the energy must be ≥ the threshold energy and the molecules must have proper orientation; rate = P Z_{AB} e^{−E_a/RT}.
